tasks.title: Implement GET /groups Endpoint with Pagination
tasks.description: Create the API endpoint to retrieve a paginated list of all groups the current authenticated user is a member of, as specified in FS-001.
tasks.details:
In `moneynote/routers/groups.py`, add a new route for `GET /groups`.
This endpoint will accept optional query parameters `page: int = 0` and `size: int = 100`.
It should depend on `get_current_user` to identify the user.
The router will call a new service method, e.g., `group_service.get_user_groups(db: Session, user_id: int, page: int, size: int)`. 
This service method will in turn call a new CRUD function, `crud_group.get_multi_by_user_id(db, user_id, offset, limit)`, which executes the SQL join between `t_user_group` and `t_user_group_user` as defined in the PRD.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that a 200 OK response is returned. Create a test user and associate them with multiple groups. Call the endpoint and assert that the response contains the correct number of groups and that the group data is accurate. Test pagination by setting `page` and `size` and verifying the subset of results. Test the case where a user belongs to zero groups, expecting an empty list.

tasks.title: Implement PUT /groups/{id} Endpoint for Group Updates
tasks.description: Develop the endpoint to allow a group owner to update the details of a specific group, including its name, notes, default currency, and default book (FS-002).
tasks.details:
In `moneynote/schemas/group.py`, define a `GroupUpdate` Pydantic model with fields: `name: str`, `notes: Optional[str]`, `defaultCurrencyCode: str`, `defaultBookId: int`.
In `moneynote/routers/groups.py`, add a `PUT /groups/{id}` route. It will call a `group_service.update_group` method.
The service method must perform the following logic within a single database transaction:
1. Retrieve the group by `id`.
2. Verify the `current_user.id` matches the group's `owner_id`. If not, raise `HTTPException(status_code=403)`.
3. Before updating, check for name conflicts with other groups owned by the same user, as per the PRD's SQL logic. If a conflict exists, raise `HTTPException(status_code=409)`.
4. Update the group object with the new data from the `GroupUpdate` model and commit the transaction.
tasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests based on TC-P4-02 and TC-P4-03. Test the happy path where an owner successfully updates a group. Test the 403 Forbidden case by having a non-owner attempt an update. Test the 409 Conflict case by trying to rename a group to a name that already exists for that user. Test the 404 Not Found case for a non-existent group ID.

tasks.title: Implement DELETE /groups/{id} Endpoint with Validation
tasks.description: Create the endpoint to delete a group, ensuring that deletion is blocked if the group still contains books (FS-003).
tasks.details:
In `moneynote/routers/groups.py`, add a `DELETE /groups/{id}` route that returns a `204 No Content` on success.
It will call a `group_service.delete_group` method.
The service method must execute the following logic in an atomic transaction:
1. Fetch the group by `id`.
2. Verify the `current_user.id` is the `owner_id`. If not, raise `HTTPException(status_code=403)`.
3. Execute a count query on `t_user_book` where `group_id` matches. If the count > 0, raise `HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Group cannot be deleted as it still contains books.")`.
4. If the check passes, delete all corresponding entries from the `t_user_group_user` association table.
5. Delete the group from the `t_user_group` table.
6. Commit the transaction.
tasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests based on TC-P4-04 and TC-P4-05. Create a group with at least one book and verify that a DELETE request returns 409 Conflict. Create an empty group, delete it, and verify the response is 204 No Content and that the group and its user associations are removed from the database.

tasks.title: Create Pydantic Schemas and CRUD functions for Book Management
tasks.description: Define the necessary Pydantic response models and create the dynamic CRUD function required for querying books.
tasks.details:
In `moneynote/schemas/book.py`, ensure a `BookDetails` schema exists that matches the fields of the `t_user_book` table for use in response models.
In `moneynote/crud/crud_book.py`, implement a new function: `get_multi_by_group_filtered(db: Session, group_id: int, filters: dict, sort: str, offset: int, limit: int)`. This function will dynamically build a SQLAlchemy query based on the `filters` dictionary which may contain `name` (for a LIKE search) and `enable` (for a boolean match). It will apply sorting, limit, and offset before executing.
tasks.testStrategy: This is a non-endpoint task. Validate through unit tests for the `crud_book.get_multi_by_group_filtered` function. Test that it correctly builds the WHERE clause when `name` and `enable` filters are provided, both separately and together. Test that it returns an empty list for non-matching filters.

tasks.title: Implement GET /books Endpoint with Filtering and Pagination
tasks.description: Develop the primary endpoint for listing books within the user's currently active group, with support for filtering and pagination (FS-004).
tasks.details:
In `moneynote/routers/books.py`, add a `GET /books` route. This route must have a dependency that provides the `active_group_id` for the current user (e.g., `get_current_active_group_id`).
It will accept optional query parameters: `enable: Optional[bool]`, `name: Optional[str]`, `page: int`, `size: int`, `sort: Optional[str]`.
The endpoint will call a `book_service.query_books` method, passing the active group ID and all filter/pagination parameters. The service will use the `crud_book.get_multi_by_group_filtered` function created in the previous task to fetch the data.
tasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests based on TC-P4-06. Set up a test user with an active group and populate it with several books. Test fetching all books. Test filtering by `name` and verify only matching books are returned. Test filtering by `enable=true` and `enable=false` and check results. Verify pagination works as expected.

tasks.title: Implement GET /books/{id} Endpoint for Book Details
tasks.description: Create the endpoint to retrieve the complete details for a single, specific book, ensuring the book belongs to the user's active group (FS-005).
tasks.details:
In `moneynote/routers/books.py`, add a `GET /books/{id}` route.
This route must also depend on `get_current_active_group_id`.
It will call a `book_service.get_book_details` method, passing the `book_id` and `active_group_id`.
The service method will fetch the book from `crud_book.get(id=book_id)`. After fetching, it MUST validate that `book.group_id == active_group_id`. If they do not match, it must raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Book not found")` to prevent leaking information about the existence of books in other groups.
tasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests based on TC-P4-07 and TC-P4-08. Test the happy path by requesting a book that exists within the user's active group, expecting a 200 OK and correct data. Test the 404 Not Found case by requesting a non-existent book ID. Crucially, test the security case by requesting a book ID that exists but belongs to a different group, and assert that the response is 404 Not Found.

tasks.title: Implement Centralized Exception Handling
tasks.description: Create a FastAPI exception handler to catch common errors like 404, 403, and 409 and return them in a standardized JSON error format.
tasks.details:
In `main.py`, add a custom exception handler for `HTTPException`.
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
from fastapi.exceptions import HTTPException

app = FastAPI()

@app.exception_handler(HTTPException)
async def http_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: HTTPException):
    return JSONResponse(
        status_code=exc.status_code,
        content={"detail": exc.detail},
    )
```
Ensure this handler is registered with the FastAPI app instance. This will standardize error responses across all endpoints implemented in this phase, matching the format `{"detail": "Error message"}`.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually trigger different HTTPExceptions from an endpoint (e.g., by requesting a non-existent ID for a 404, or attempting an action as a non-owner for a 403). Verify that the response body for all errors consistently follows the `{"detail": "..."}` JSON structure and that the status code is correct.

tasks.title: Documentation Update for Phase 4 Endpoints
tasks.description: Update the project's API documentation (e.g., Swagger/OpenAPI docs) to reflect the newly added GET, PUT, and DELETE endpoints for Groups and Books.
tasks.details: Review the auto-generated OpenAPI documentation served by FastAPI at `/docs`. For each new endpoint, ensure the Pydantic models and FastAPI route declarations generate clear and accurate documentation. Add `description` and `summary` arguments to the FastAPI route decorators (`@router.get`, `@router.put`, etc.) to provide context for each endpoint's purpose, parameters, and possible responses as outlined in the PRD.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the application locally and navigate to the `/docs` URL. Review the sections for `groups` and `books`. Verify that all new endpoints (`GET /groups`, `PUT /groups/{id}`, `DELETE /groups/{id}`, `GET /books`, `GET /books/{id}`) are present. Check that request bodies, query parameters, and response models are correctly documented.
